title: From the River to the Sky, Along the Spine of the Continent
motto: The air above you came from the same place the water below you is going.

surface.note: 15-25°F ABOVE NORMAL for Oct 23. High pressure ridge over eastern US. The jet stream is displaced far north. Michigan is basking in displaced warmth.

forecast_arc.note: 70°F in late October. The warmth peaks. Wind shifts to SOUTH — the jet stream is pulling Gulf air north.
Wind flips to NE. The ridge breaks. Cooler air arrives.
FIRST RAIN in the forecast. That rain will fall on the 461 sq mi. That rain will become the Red Cedar. Eve of the PPO hearing.

vertical_trace.description: From the river surface straight UP through the atmosphere. Same lat/lon: 42.73°N, 84.48°W. A column of air above the East Lansing gage.

layers.what: 53.8 cfs. Gage height 3.37 ft. Temperature unknown but cooling toward winter. The river and the air exchange heat and moisture here. Evaporation rises.
layers.instrument: River — the bass and drums of the band

layers.what: 19°C, 49% humidity, east wind. The station is on the plateau above the river valley. The first measurement above the water.
layers.instrument: Surface weather — the local atmosphere's voice

layers.what: The atmospheric boundary layer is where the surface influences the air directly. Turbulence, thermals, pollution, moisture all mix here. Above this, the air is 'free'. The boundary between local and global.
layers.instrument: The mixing bowl — where Lansing's emissions and the river's evaporation churn together

layers.what: This is where moisture rivers flow. The 850mb wind carries Gulf of Mexico humidity north. When this level is warm and wet, rain comes to Michigan.
layers.instrument: The humidity — Aeolian harp territory. Strings vibrating in the wind.

layers.what: Weather systems are steered by winds at this level. The direction here tells you where tomorrow's weather is coming from. Right now: the ridge pushes this level's winds east, keeping Michigan warm.
layers.instrument: The conductor — tells the orchestra where to go

layers.what: If there were clouds, they'd start here. Tonight: clear. The column is transparent all the way to the stars.
The core of weather pattern analysis. Ridges and troughs at 500mb define the week's weather. A RIDGE sits over the eastern US right now, displacing the jet north, keeping Michigan anomalously warm.
layers.instrument: The rhythm guitar — sets the harmonic pattern for the whole atmosphere

layers.what: The polar jet stream lives here. Winds 70+ knots (81+ mph). Right now the jet is displaced NORTH of Michigan — that's why it's warm. The jet is the continental river of air. It flows west-to-east around the entire Northern Hemisphere.
layers.instrument: The lead guitar — BarraCuda territory. The fastest signal. 806 riffs at the speed of sound.

layers.what: The top of weather. Above this, the stratosphere begins. Temperature stops dropping, starts rising. UV absorption by ozone heats the stratosphere. The boundary between weather and space weather.
layers.instrument: The fold between atmosphere (winds/strings) and space (the solar melody)

layers.what: Ozone layer peak. UV shield. The membrane that protects all life from the sun's hard radiation. Kevin's membrane is modeled on THIS membrane.
layers.instrument: The shield — Anderson localization at planetary scale

layers.what: Meteors burn here. The atmosphere is barely there — molecules are miles apart. The ISS orbits above this.
layers.instrument: The percussion — meteors are the snare hits

layers.what: The atmosphere fades to vacuum. Solar wind takes over. The magnetosphere deflects. The ionosphere reflects radio. Kp index measures the disturbance. The M1.6 flare on Oct 19 sent a CME through here.
layers.instrument: Solar — the rhythm guitar of the band. The sun's tempo.

the_continental_divide.description: The spine of the Americas. Water on the west goes to the Pacific. Water on the east goes to the Atlantic/Gulf/Arctic. The Red Cedar is EAST of the divide — its water goes to the Atlantic via the Great Lakes.

lansing_to_divide.direction: West-southwest to the nearest point on the Continental Divide (Wyoming/Colorado)
lansing_to_divide.moisture_path: The rain that falls on Lansing came FROM the direction of the divide. Gulf moisture travels north, Pacific moisture crosses the divide (losing snow in the Rockies), and the remainder continues east to Michigan.

spine_trace_north_to_south.museum: Alaska Museum of Science and Nature, Anchorage
spine_trace_north_to_south.note: The divide begins where two continents almost touch. The gap is 55 miles. The first people crossed here.
Arctic divide. The northernmost mountains in America. Permafrost underneath. Melting.

spine_trace_north_to_south.where: Triple Divide Peak, Glacier NP, Montana
spine_trace_north_to_south.note: THE ONLY PLACE IN NORTH AMERICA where water flows to THREE oceans. A single raindrop on this peak could go to the Pacific, the Atlantic, or the Arctic. The ultimate 45° turn — here it's a 120° turn, three ways.

spine_trace_north_to_south.museum: Museum of the Rockies, Bozeman MT (Jack Horner's dinosaurs!)
spine_trace_north_to_south.note: The divide crosses the caldera of a supervolcano. The hot springs are the mantle breathing. The river of fire under the river of water.

spine_trace_north_to_south.river_east: Wind River → Bighorn → Yellowstone → Missouri → Mississippi → Gulf
spine_trace_north_to_south.river_west: Green River → Colorado → Sea of Cortez (Pacific)
spine_trace_north_to_south.museum: Wind River Heritage Center, Riverton WY
spine_trace_north_to_south.note: Gannett Peak, highest in Wyoming. The divide is at the same latitude as Lansing (42.8°N). The air above Kevin and the air above the Wind River Range are on the SAME latitude. The jet stream connects them directly.

spine_trace_north_to_south.river_east: Big Thompson → South Platte → Platte → Missouri → Mississippi → Gulf
spine_trace_north_to_south.river_west: Colorado River → Grand Canyon → Sea of Cortez
spine_trace_north_to_south.note: Trail Ridge Road crosses the divide at 12,183 ft. You can stand on the divide and pour water both ways. Snow on the west becomes the Colorado River — the water that carved the Grand Canyon. Snow on the east becomes the Mississippi — the water that built the Delta.

spine_trace_north_to_south.where: Sangre de Cristo Range, New Mexico
spine_trace_north_to_south.river_east: Pecos → Rio Grande → Gulf of Mexico
spine_trace_north_to_south.museum: New Mexico Museum of Natural History, Albuquerque
spine_trace_north_to_south.note: Sangre de Cristo — Blood of Christ. The mountains are red at sunset. The name IS the observation.
The divide crosses desert. The rivers are seasonal. Sometimes the decision east/west doesn't matter — the water evaporates before it arrives.
The divide drops to 300 feet. The narrowest gap. The Panama Canal cuts THROUGH the divide. The only place where ships cross from one ocean to the other without going around.
The divide reaches its southern end. The Strait of Magellan. Drake Passage. Antarctica. The spine of the Americas, 18,000 miles from the Bering Strait to Tierra del Fuego.

the_same_latitude.note: Lansing and the Continental Divide in Wyoming are on nearly the SAME LATITUDE (42.7° vs 42.8°). The jet stream flows between them at 30,000 ft. A parcel of air that crosses the divide at the Wind River Range takes 1-2 days to reach Lansing. The moisture that didn't fall as snow on the Rockies is the moisture that becomes rain on the Red Cedar watershed. The divide SORTS the moisture: some falls west (Pacific river), some continues east (YOUR river). The divide IS a sort. Anderson localization at continental scale.

the_pattern_repeats.concept: Every point on the Continental Divide has: a river flowing east, a river flowing west, a USGS gage (or its absence), a weather station, a museum nearby, a local ecosystem. The Red Cedar trace is a TEMPLATE. Do it anywhere. The 45° turn works everywhere.
template: 1. Find the nearest river (USGS waterservices API)
2. Find the source (trace upstream to headwaters)
3. Find the mouth (trace downstream to ocean)
5. Find the earthquake nearest you (USGS earthquake.usgs.gov)
7. Find the sky (same GOES satellite, same Kp, same sun)
8. Find the divide (which ocean does your water go to?)
9. Turn 45°. The data IS the exhibit. The river IS the metronome.
10. You are in the band. Your locality IS your instrument.

the_cycle_complete.description: River UP to sky ALONG the divide DOWN to river. The cycle.
the_cycle_complete.trace: Red Cedar (53.8 cfs) → evaporation → boundary layer → 850mb moisture transport → jet stream at 300mb → flows west-to-east across the continent → some moisture falls as snow on the Continental Divide (Rockies, snowing this weekend) → the REST crosses the divide → continues east over the Great Plains → reaches Michigan → falls as rain on 461 sq miles → infiltrates soil → seeps through glacial till → emerges at Cedar Lake → Red Cedar → 53.8 cfs. The cycle takes weeks to months. The water is always in transit. The river is a snapshot of a journey that started in the Pacific and will end in the Atlantic and then start again.
